summary: Guidance for separating long-lived SSE heartbeat credits from high-throughput bulk embedding jobs
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports frequent 429s that correlate with simultaneous long-lived SSE (server-sent events) sessions used to stream small inference outputs and a parallel bulk embedding pipeline that performs high-throughput multipart uploads. Impact: Intermittent client errors (HTTP 429) for SSE listeners (real-time dashboards) and occasional queue rejection for bulk workers. Business effect: dashboards lose near-real-time updates and some embedding batches are retried, increasing processing latency and cost.

Environment: Dedicated tenancy in prod-us-east. Multiple API keys in use: one ephemeral key per dashboard instance (SSE), a pool of worker keys for bulk embedding jobs. Traffic pattern: ~120 concurrent SSE connections per customer region, heartbeat/ping every 55s; bulk pipeline kicks off 150 parallel multipart upload workers during ETL windows.

Steps to reproduce: 1) Open 100+ SSE clients against the streaming route with default keepalive. 2) Start bulk embedding job orchestration to upload 1000 small files in concurrent chunks with 150 workers. 3) Observe rate-limit headers and 429 responses on both SSE route and /v1/embeddings endpoints.

Observed behavior: 429s surface mostly on SSE reconnects and on short-lived preflight /status checks from workers. Rate-limit response headers show route-window exhaustion and tenant-level token deficit. Console shows burst credits dropping to zero quickly during overlapping windows.

Expected behavior: Long-lived SSE sessions should consume a small steady share (or be isolated) and not drive short-window burst exhaustion that impacts bulk ingest. Bulk jobs should be able to use a separate burst lane or be queued gracefully if tenant tokens are exhausted.

Attachments: sample headers, condensed metrics snapshot, small HAR from a dashboard client (attached in ticket).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start 120 SSE clients to /v1/streams/subscribe with keepalive enabled. 2) Trigger bulk ingest workflow with 150 parallel workers hitting /v1/embeddings in chunked mode. 3) Watch for 429 responses within 2-5 minutes and note X-RateLimit-* headers. 4) Reproduce is more likely if bulk jobs start just after SSE sessions have established (overlapping refill windows).
logs:
[2026-03-09T14:03:21Z] proxy: connID=4483 keepalive ping sent; [2026-03-09T14:03:22Z] rate-limiter: tenant=dsift burst=0 window=10s refill=100; [2026-03-09T14:03:23Z] embed-worker-12: upload chunk 5/42 -> 429; X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0; [2026-03-09T14:03:27Z] sse-client-93: reconnect attempt -> 429

Metrics observed: token_refill_rate 100/min, tenant_consumption_spike coincident with ETL start, burst_pool_depletion timeline matches SSE heartbeat windows.
comments: 2026-03-09 Priya Sharma (Support): Customer reports recurring 429 waves when dashboards and batch ingest overlap. They request recommended config to avoid mutual interference.
2026-03-09 Ethan Cole (SRE): Acknowledged. Asked for sample rate-limit headers and timeseries for token buckets; requested a short window of logs (14:00-14:10).
2026-03-10 DataSift Ops (customer): Uploaded HAR and metrics. Added that SSE heartbeats are configurable but default heartbeat is 55s. Bulk window starts at 14:00 UTC nightly.

2026-03-10 Ethan Cole (SRE): Initial hypothesis: heartbeat preflight and small periodic probe traffic (from SSE clients) is being counted against the same burst pool as bulk workers. Suggested two mitigation options in next comment.

2026-03-10 Ethan Cole (SRE): Suggested mitigations: (1) Isolate long-lived connections by assigning them a separate route with dedicated burst pool (console/private config) and increase SSE keepalive interval to 90s as short-term. (2) For bulk, schedule staggered worker startup and use worker-level rate-smoothing (client side). Requested permission to propose a dedicated burst lane configuration for their dedicated tenancy.
investigation_notes: Checked console token-bucket traces: tenant-level burst pool shows repeated full drains during ETL window; per-route counters spike for /v1/embeddings and /v1/streams/subscribe simultaneously.
Confirmed X-RateLimit headers map to route-window exhaustion rather than gateway errors; no 5xx correlation in same window.
Hypothesis A: SSE heartbeat probes are counted as individual short requests causing many small debits across the bucket during each refill tick, amplifying sawtooth pattern.
Hypothesis B: Worker pool uses many short-lived ephemeral keys; ephemeral key fanout expands token accounting and reduces effective burst capacity for the tenant.
Ran quick test in staging by isolating SSE traffic onto a dedicated route: observed zero 429s for bulk jobs in that run.
resolution_notes: Workaround applied: temporarily configured an isolated route for SSE traffic (dedicated burst pool) and advised DataSift to increase client keepalive to 90s and enable client-side staggering for worker startup. We also recommended a console change: provision a secondary burst pool for long-lived streaming listeners in their Dedicated tenancy. Follow-up: engineering to evaluate making per-connection heartbeat probes exempt from tenant-level short-window accounting (RFC required).
next_steps: Schedule a joint runbook session with DataSift Ops to apply recommended console settings and test for 72 hours.
ENG: Create RFC to evaluate 'heartbeat-exempt' probe classification in rate-limiter (linked PR candidate).
Support: Monitor tenant-level bucket depletion metrics and re-open ticket if 429s recur after configuration change.
